name: wget
summary: Download files from the web, within the web access the application allows
help: Usage: wget [OPTION]... [URL]...
Download each URL to a file named after it (or as -O says), following redirects.
-O,  --output-document=FILE   write to FILE; '-' writes to standard output
-q,  --quiet                  print nothing but errors that end the run
-nv, --no-verbose             one line per download instead of the full report
-P,  --directory-prefix=DIR   save files under DIR
-nc, --no-clobber             skip a download whose file already exists
--spider                 only check that each URL exists; download nothing
-t,  --tries=NUM              accepted and ignored: Topwater tries once
--show-progress          accepted and ignored: no progress bar is printed
-S,  --server-response        print the response headers
--header=STRING          add a request header ("Name: value")
--post-data=STRING       send STRING in a POST body
--post-file=FILE         send FILE in a POST body
-U,  --user-agent=AGENT       set the User-Agent header
-T,  --timeout=SECONDS        give up after SECONDS
--max-redirect=NUM       follow at most NUM redirects
--no-check-certificate   accepted and ignored: certificates are always verified
-h,  --help                   show this help
-V,  --version                show the version
The application decides which sites can be reached; others fail like an unknown host.

options.description: write every response body to FILE ('-': standard output)
print each response's status line and headers on standard error
send a POST with STRING as its body
send a POST with FILE's contents as its body
time limit for each request (the policy's limit still applies)
the most redirects to follow (never more than the policy allows)
accepted and ignored: certificates are always verified
report each download in one line, and errors (also written -nv)
save files under DIR, created if missing (ignored with -O)
do not download a URL whose file already exists, and never save as NAME.1 (also written -nc)
send HEAD for each URL and report whether it exists (exit status 8 if not); nothing is saved
accepted and ignored: each URL is tried once
accepted and ignored: no progress bar is printed

exitCodes.1: generic error (an output file that cannot be written, a request the web policy refuses)
exitCodes.4: network failure: host not resolved or not allowed, connection refused, timeout, a response cut short or unreadable
exitCodes.8: the server answered with an error status, or too many redirects

messages.resolve: wget: unable to resolve host address {host:locale}
messages.closed: {time} - Connection closed at byte {size}. Giving up.
messages.timeout: Read error (Connection timed out) in headers.
messages.recv: Read error (Connection reset by peer) in headers.
messages.tooLarge: wget: the response is larger than the web policy allows ({limit} bytes)
messages.blocked: wget: blocked by the web policy: {reason}
messages.replay: wget: Topwater replay: {request} is not in the recording
messages.spiderMode: Spider mode enabled. Check if remote file exists.
messages.spiderMissing: Remote file does not exist -- broken link!!!

notes: Registered in every shell; without a web policy every host fails to resolve. The progress report is shortened: no Resolving/Connecting lines, no dots or speed. No retries. -nv and -nc are wget's two-letter short forms of --no-verbose and --no-clobber. A body cut short (before its Content-Length or last chunk) is written as far as it came and fails with 4; a chunk size that is not hex, an unreadable status line or header, and no response at all fail with 4 and write nothing (wget itself reads some of these as HTTP/0.9 or skips the line).
